items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: I know it was painted black because I followed Earl and the paint came off on my shirt.

ctx.x: Now, as Buddy later explained it to me, it was something might have happened at that moment, forget it, it'll be all right the next moment. Murphy didn't take it that way, that he's not worrying about the rhythm. So they stopped talking. And they stopped talking -- Murphy didn't want to stand near him. And now the boss is looking at me because I got to put the bass in front of the piano. I'm the leader and the bass player is standing right in front of me so he can get away from the drummer. I can't explain to him…

And it was ridiculous and I couldn't cure it. Well, finally, the Continental -- Bob did leave for a stretch and they put Earl Hines in. And now, there's a story I want to tell about that. Earl Hines is coming in, we got to get a piano. They had an upright Kimball and it was a gas but now we got to get a grand for Earl, right? Spending $4100 a week on music, got to get a grand. Of course, that included the other gypsy band that was playing in the other room or something.
